candidate.title: Does residual sugar modify the alcohol–quality association within wine color?
candidate.question: Within red and white wines separately, is the association between alcohol and sensory quality more positive at higher residual sugar, after accounting for the other measured physicochemical variables and restricting comparisons to overlapping composition ranges?

core.relation_or_action: Estimate alcohol-by-residual-sugar interaction in an ordinal quality model, with color-specific terms and adjustment for the other measured chemistry
core.contrast: Alcohol–quality slope at higher versus lower residual sugar within each color, compared with a model lacking the interaction
core.prediction: The alcohol–quality association will be more positive at higher residual sugar in at least one color; this is an observational prediction, not a sugar intervention effect
core.independent_unit: Wine sample row; whether rows represent independent lots is unknown

candidate.failure_condition: The interaction is negligible or inconsistent across colors, lacks support within common composition ranges, or disappears under reasonable model and influence checks.
assumptions: The quality score has an ordinal interpretation.
Measured covariates and common-support restriction address only measured composition; unmeasured style and producer effects may remain.
A row is a suitable analysis unit, though independence across rows is unverified.
candidate.required_new_data: None for an observational test. Causal interpretation would require randomized sugar and alcohol manipulations with blinded panel ratings.
candidate.domain_value: A reproducible interaction could motivate testing whether composition-specific sensory guidance differs by wine style; a null result would discourage treating a pooled alcohol association as a balance rule.
candidate.discriminating_delta: Tests a specific non-additive alcohol–sugar relation within color, rather than predicting quality from a list of variables or assuming an intervention effect.

final.what_changed: The proposed observational comparison remains untested. Compute C1 failed during JSON serialization because quality_levels contained a NumPy int64; it returned no model estimates, fit comparison, or row counts. Search S1 failed on two SSL connection attempts and returned no literature evidence. These failures block empirical and nearest-work assessment; they do not support or refute the forecast.
final.what_is_known: The supplied dataset has 6,497 rows and includes red and white samples, quality scores, and 11 measured chemistry variables. Its metadata reports no missing values and notes that producer and other provenance information are unavailable. No result from C1 or S1 is available.
final.new_hypothesis: None; retain the original observational interaction hypothesis without treating it as supported.
final.next_falsifiable_test: Rerun the prespecified proportional-odds comparison after converting NumPy scalar outputs to native JSON types. Report optimizer status, color-specific interaction estimates and uncertainty, row counts, and sensitivity to influence and support definitions. Retry a targeted literature search before making a novelty claim.
final.nearest_work_comparison: The bundle identifies the dataset and its associated 2009 paper, but does not establish whether that or other work tested this color-specific alcohol-by-residual-sugar interaction. The targeted search failed, so the nearest-work comparison is unresolved.
final.novelty_status: Unverified. The dataset is recognized; metadata is not a discovery, and the failed search cannot establish novelty.

candidate.title: Do alcohol–sugar interaction terms improve ordinal quality fit within wine color?
candidate.question: Within the supplied wine samples, do prespecified nonlinear alcohol-by-residual_sugar terms improve proportional-odds model fit beyond linear chemistry terms and quadratic alcohol and residual_sugar main effects, allowing the interaction surface to differ by color?

core.object: Row-level quality scores and physicochemical measurements for red and white vinho verde samples
core.relation_or_action: Compare proportional-odds models with the same linear chemistry terms and quadratic alcohol and residual_sugar terms, with or without six color-specific interaction terms
core.contrast: In-sample ordinal log likelihood for the expanded interaction model versus the additive quadratic model on rows within each color's marginal 5th–95th percentile ranges
core.prediction: The expanded model will improve in-sample fit, but this comparison alone will not establish a positive interaction over a well-supported region or a causal sensory effect.
core.independent_unit: Wine sample row; independent lot or panelist structure is unknown

candidate.failure_condition: The interaction model fails to converge or does not improve fit under a prespecified, dependence-aware validation and sensitivity analysis.
assumptions: Quality is treated as ordinal under a proportional-odds model.
The quadratic specification is an approximation, not a general flexible surface.
Marginal percentile filtering does not guarantee joint composition support.
Row-level observations may be dependent, and measured chemistry does not control unmeasured production or style factors.
candidate.required_new_data: None for a further row-level model comparison; independent lots and blinded sensory ratings are needed for lot-level or causal claims.
candidate.domain_value: Tests whether a specific nonlinear interaction adds conditional fit beyond curvature in the two main effects, informing whether a separately designed sensory experiment is warranted.
candidate.discriminating_delta: Replaces a directional claim about a positive association in a post hoc region with a prespecified comparison of nonlinear interaction terms against quadratic main effects.

final.what_changed: C2 successfully fit both models on 5,432 rows (4,107 white; 1,325 red); both optimizers reported convergence. The expanded model had nll 5761.204 versus 5786.665 for the additive model, giving a nominal 6-df likelihood-ratio statistic of 50.922 (approximate p=3.07e-9). This is in-sample model-fit evidence for the specified added terms, not evidence that the alcohol–quality association shifts positively in a particular region. The forecast about a positive shift and weaker interaction after nonlinear adjustment is therefore unresolved. S2 failed twice with SSL errors and supplied no literature evidence.
final.what_is_known: C2 reports quality levels 3–9 and a within-color marginal 5th–95th percentile filter for alcohol and residual_sugar. The filter does not establish joint support. The model comparison is observational, has no independent-lot metadata, and provides no coefficient uncertainty or dependence-aware validation. The supplied dataset documentation notes missing producer and other provenance information.
final.new_hypothesis: The six specified interaction terms may improve conditional ordinal fit in these rows, but the direction and stability of the implied alcohol–quality association shift across residual_sugar remain unknown.
final.next_falsifiable_test: Evaluate the prespecified interaction surface with uncertainty over a declared joint-support region, then check it under row-influence and dependence-aware sensitivity analyses. For causal interpretation, randomize alcohol and sugar levels across independent base wine lots and collect blinded repeated panel ratings.
final.nearest_work_comparison: The bundle identifies the dataset and its associated 2009 paper, but does not establish whether prior work tested this nonlinear, color-specific interaction. S2 failed, so comparison of outcome, interaction specification, color stratification, and sampling unit remains unresolved.
final.novelty_status: Unverified. Recognition of the dataset and the computed fit difference do not establish novelty; the targeted search returned no evidence.

candidate.title: Does the volatile_acidity association vary across quality thresholds?
candidate.question: Among the supplied wine samples, does the adjusted volatile_acidity association with quality vary across cumulative score thresholds, and is it weaker at thresholds for higher scores?

core.object: Row-level ordinal quality scores and measured chemistry for red and white wine samples
core.relation_or_action: Estimate threshold-specific volatile_acidity slopes with a prespecified partial proportional-odds model, retaining common slopes for other covariates
core.contrast: A common volatile_acidity slope versus threshold-varying slopes on identical rows and covariates
core.prediction: The negative association may attenuate at higher quality thresholds; the supplied exploratory fits show this pattern descriptively, but do not establish it.
core.independent_unit: Wine sample row; lot, producer, and panelist dependence are unknown

candidate.failure_condition: A converged, prespecified model finds no meaningful threshold variation, or the pattern is unstable under influence and color-stratified sensitivity checks.
assumptions: Quality scores have an ordinal interpretation, but their panel measurement process is undocumented.
The model handles cumulative probabilities without crossing and uses the same rows and covariates across comparisons.
Row-level estimates do not establish intervention effects or independent-lot generalization.
candidate.required_new_data: None for a row-level model comparison. Panelist and lot identifiers are needed to assess dependence and generalization; causal claims require randomized acidity manipulation and blinded ratings.
candidate.domain_value: Could distinguish whether volatile_acidity relates similarly to avoiding low ratings and reaching high ratings, rather than relying on one average ordinal association.
candidate.discriminating_delta: Examines whether a measured chemical association changes across outcome thresholds, a different question from the prior alcohol–residual_sugar interaction.

final.what_changed: C3 returned six separate cumulative-logit estimates on 6,497 rows. The volatile_acidity coefficients became less negative from lower to higher thresholds: -0.854 at quality >3, -0.903 at >4, -0.787 at >5, -0.603 at >6, -0.292 at >7, and -0.213 at >8. This descriptively opposes the forecast of a more negative association at higher thresholds. Five fits reported precision loss; the threshold >8 fit had only five observations above the threshold and a model-based SE of 0.865. These exploratory fits do not provide a formal test of threshold variation. Search S3 returned general ordinal-model references, not wine-specific evidence about volatile_acidity or this dataset.
final.what_is_known: The data contain 6,497 rows and quality levels 3–9. C3's six threshold fits reuse the same rows, and their reported standard errors assume independent rows. The dataset lacks panelist, producer, vintage, and lot identifiers. S3's scope is Crossref metadata and is not exhaustive.
final.new_hypothesis: The negative volatile_acidity association may attenuate at higher quality thresholds, but sparse upper categories and optimization precision loss could produce an unstable pattern.
final.next_falsifiable_test: Fit a converged partial proportional-odds model with only the volatile_acidity slope varying by threshold, check cumulative-probability ordering, report threshold-specific uncertainty and category counts, and assess influence and color-stratified sensitivity. If convergence or category sparsity prevents reliable estimation, report that limitation rather than treating separate threshold fits as confirmation.
final.nearest_work_comparison: S3 found general methods on partial proportional odds and proportionality assessment, including DOI 10.2307/2532457, but no returned wine-specific study. Comparison by wine outcome, volatile_acidity relation, threshold model, and sampling unit remains unresolved.
final.novelty_status: Unverified. Dataset recognition and the returned general-method references do not establish novelty.

candidate.title: How much quality disagreement remains among chemically similar wines?
candidate.question: Within each color, do wines paired by nearest-neighbor distance across the 11 measured physicochemical variables have smaller absolute quality-score differences than a reference formed by permuting quality within coarse chemistry strata?

core.object: Absolute difference in observed quality scores between paired wine samples
core.relation_or_action: Relate multivariate physicochemical similarity to quality-score agreement
core.contrast: Observed mean absolute quality difference for unique nearest-neighbor pairs versus within-stratum quality-permutation values
core.prediction: Nearest-neighbor pairs show smaller score differences than the permutation reference in both colors, while their mean score difference remains above zero.
core.independent_unit: A wine row; pairs share rows, and lot, producer, and panel identifiers are unavailable.

candidate.failure_condition: Nearest-neighbor disagreement is not lower than the permutation reference in either color, or the result depends strongly on the chosen distance or strata.
assumptions: Z-scaled Euclidean distance across the 11 measured variables is a useful chemistry-similarity measure.
Permuting quality within the 16 PCA-quartile strata provides a descriptive reference; its interpretation depends on within-stratum exchangeability.
The dataset does not identify sampling clusters or sources of score variation.
candidate.required_new_data: For validation, independently sampled wines with lot and producer identifiers, repeated blinded sensory ratings, and the same physicochemical measurements.
candidate.domain_value: Estimates whether measured chemistry is locally associated with quality scores and whether appreciable score disagreement remains among chemically similar samples.
candidate.discriminating_delta: Tests local chemistry-score concordance against a conditional permutation reference, rather than a specific chemical interaction or a red-white score gap.

final.what_changed: The requested computation ran successfully. In both colors, observed nearest-neighbor score disagreement was below the 500-permutation reference interval: red 0.381 versus mean 0.631 (95% permutation interval 0.602–0.661), and white 0.373 versus mean 0.714 (0.695–0.732). None of the 500 permutations was as favorable as the observed value in either color. The forecasted direction was observed. The search returned broad wine sensory-analysis and instrumental-assessment sources, but its Crossref metadata scope is not exhaustive and does not resolve whether this exact question has been studied.
final.what_is_known: For the specified scaling, nearest-neighbor rule, and PCA-quartile strata, chemically nearest pairs had lower mean absolute quality-score differences than the permutation references. Their observed disagreement was still nonzero. Pair counts were 1,350 red and 4,241 white; the 16 strata per color had minimum sizes 66 and 269, respectively. Pair counts are not independent replication. The permutation comparison assumes within-stratum exchangeability and does not account for unknown lot, producer, or panel structure. These results describe association in this dataset; they do not show that chemistry is sufficient, explain disagreement, or establish sensory-rating reliability.
final.new_hypothesis: Measured chemistry contains local information about quality scores beyond the coarse PCA-quartile permutation reference, while additional unmeasured factors or score variation may contribute to the remaining disagreement. This dataset cannot distinguish those explanations.
final.next_falsifiable_test: Evaluate the prespecified distance and reference on independently sampled wines with lot and producer identifiers and repeated blinded ratings. Before collection, specify the chemistry-distance rule, score-disagreement outcome, and comparison; test whether the lower disagreement among nearest neighbors replicates and estimate how much variation is attributable to batches and raters.
final.nearest_work_comparison: The supplied dataset documentation describes physicochemical modeling of quality and mentions feature relevance and outlier detection. The returned sources include general sensory analysis and instrumental assessment of wine, but no abstracts establishing whether they test local multivariate chemistry similarity against score disagreement. The result therefore distinguishes this question from the supplied general modeling objective only; it does not establish a literature gap.
final.novelty_status: Unverified. The search was limited to Crossref metadata and returned broad sources without enough detail to establish overlap or novelty.

candidate.title: Is product-page duration share nonlinearly associated with Revenue?
candidate.question: Among sessions with positive total recorded category duration, does ProductRelated_Duration divided by total recorded category duration show a nonlinear conditional association with Revenue after accounting for total duration, page counts, Month, VisitorType, and TrafficType, excluding PageValues?

core.object: Revenue and product-page share of recorded Administrative, Informational, and ProductRelated duration
core.relation_or_action: Estimate a prespecified nonlinear conditional association between product-page duration share and Revenue
core.contrast: A nonlinear share term versus a linear share term, using the same adjustment variables and eligible sessions
core.prediction: A nonlinear share term will improve out-of-sample log loss over the linear term; the observed decile rates do not support predicting a monotonic direction.

candidate.failure_condition: The nonlinear term does not improve held-out log loss under a prespecified split and model, or its estimated pattern is unstable across reasonable specifications.
assumptions: The three duration measures are comparable enough to define their sum and a product-page share; this measurement meaning is not established by the bundle.
Sessions with zero total recorded duration are excluded, and conclusions apply only to eligible sessions.
Adjustment describes conditional association and does not establish that changing time allocation changes conversion.
The split and nonlinear model are fixed before evaluating held-out results.
required_new_data: Documentation confirming whether the three duration fields represent comparable, non-overlapping time; event-level timestamps would be needed to establish temporal ordering relative to purchase intent or transaction.
candidate.domain_value: Tests whether the recorded allocation of browsing duration contains descriptive information beyond total duration and page counts, and whether a simple linear summary is inadequate.
candidate.discriminating_delta: Prior candidates examined product dwell per page and its VisitorType interaction. This candidate examines the share of recorded category duration and compares nonlinear with linear association; it does not claim a causal reallocation effect.

final.what_changed: The actual compute return found 720 of 12,330 sessions with zero total recorded category duration, leaving 11,610 eligible sessions (9,705 Revenue=False; 1,905 Revenue=True). Revenue rates across equal-count product-share deciles were nonmonotonic, so I removed the proposed directional prediction and revised the question to test nonlinearity. No adjusted model, uncertainty estimate, or held-out comparison was returned; feasibility summaries do not establish an association.
final.what_is_known: In compute_0, product-share decile conversion rates ranged from about 0.049 to 0.250 and did not change monotonically. The share's correlation with total duration was about 0.066; its correlations with Administrative, Informational, and ProductRelated page counts were about -0.394, -0.232, and 0.118. These summaries do not establish adequate conditional overlap across categorical covariates or support for an adjusted estimate. The duration fields' measurement comparability and timing are unresolved.
final.new_hypothesis: The product-page duration share may have a nonlinear descriptive association with Revenue, but the supplied feasibility summaries neither confirm that relationship nor distinguish it from confounding, measurement structure, or selection into positive-duration sessions.
final.next_falsifiable_test: On eligible sessions, compare prespecified linear and restricted-spline product-share terms in otherwise identical models with the stated adjustment variables, excluding PageValues. Use a fixed session-level held-out split; report held-out log loss, uncertainty appropriate to the split design, overlap, and sensitivity to the zero-duration exclusion. No improvement or an unstable pattern would fail the nonlinear-association prediction.
final.nearest_work_comparison: The supplied history includes questions about ProductRelated_Duration per ProductRelated page and its interaction with VisitorType. This proposal changes the focal measure to a category-duration share and tests functional form, but remains related to those prior duration–Revenue questions. The bundle contains no current-round literature search result, so literature novelty is unverified.
final.novelty_status: Literature novelty unverified; history-relative difference is a refinement of earlier duration–Revenue candidates, not a demonstrated new family.
